title: Special Campaign 6.0: Department of Posts Achieves Significant Progress in Grievance Redressal, Cleanliness, E-Waste Disposal and Space Management
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 OCT 2026 6:57PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Posts, under the Ministry of Communications, has made significant progress during the implementation phase of Special Campaign 6, being undertaken across postal establishments throughout the country from 2nd to 31st October 2026. The campaign aims to institutionalize Swachhata, reduce pendency, promote efficient record management and ensure responsible disposal of e-waste, while improving the working environment and citizen experience at postal establishments.
Under Special Campaign 6, the Department has set ambitious targets for the resolution of 1,50,000 public grievances, disposal of 1,500 appeals and cleanliness drives at 1,35,000 sites nationwide. The campaign builds on the Department’s continued efforts towards efficient public service delivery, accountable governance and sustainable office management.
Significant Progress Till 16th October 2026
The Department has recorded the following achievements during the implementation phase:
Cleanliness Drives:
Cleanliness activities have been undertaken at 73,814 sites, including post offices, accounting for approximately 55% of the overall target of 1,35,000 sites.
Public Grievance Redressal:
A total of 1,00,214 public grievances have been resolved against the campaign target of 1,50,000, achieving approximately 67% of the target.
Appeal Disposal:
764 appeals have been disposed of against the target of 1,500, achieving approximately 51% of the target.
Scrap Disposal and Revenue Generation:
A total of 3,06,026 kg of scrap has been disposed of since 2nd October 2026, generating revenue of ₹67.56 lakh.
E-Waste Management:
In line with the campaign’s focus on scientific e-waste management, 17,980 kg of e-waste has been disposed of, generating revenue of ₹27.64 lakh. These efforts reflect the Department’s commitment to responsible handling and disposal of obsolete electronic equipment.
Innovative Initiatives: Turning Waste into Wealth
Postal Circles have also undertaken innovative initiatives to promote recycling, reuse and the productive utilization of available resources.
In West Bengal Circle, departmental carpenters and Multi-Tasking Staff (MTS) renovated the Senior Manager’s Chamber at the Mail Motor Service (MMS), Kolkata, using recycled wooden scrap. The initiative exemplifies the concept of
“Waste to Wealth”
, demonstrating how discarded materials can be creatively reused to improve office infrastructure.
Citizen-Centric Governance and Service Delivery
As part of its citizen-centric initiatives, the Department has also introduced
DigiPost
, a phygital mail service through which traffic e-challans issued by Gujarat Police are digitally transmitted for physical delivery to citizens. The initiative demonstrates the potential of the postal network to facilitate the delivery of digitally generated citizen services through its extensive physical reach.
The Department of Posts will continue to intensify its efforts during the remaining period of Special Campaign 6 to achieve the prescribed targets, sustain cleanliness practices, ensure scientific e-waste management and reinforce its commitment to responsive, efficient and citizen-centric governance.

title: Department of School Education and Literacy focuses on administrative efficiency, cleaner school campuses and responsible e-waste Management as part of Special Campaign 6
subtitle: Nationwide e-waste awareness and collection drive to be organised on October 28, 2026.
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 OCT 2026 8:37PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Department of School Education and Literacy (DoSEL), Union Ministry of Education, is actively implementing
Special Campaign 6 from Oct 2 to 31, 2026
, with a focus on improving administrative efficiency, promoting cleanliness across school campuses and strengthening responsible electronic waste (e-waste) management. The Campaign also seeks to encourage school students and communities to adopt sustainable practices.
Key focus areas under Special Campaign 6 include:
Minimising Pendency and Enhancing Efficiency in Official Work
Efforts are being undertaken across the Department and its organisations to minimise pendency in official work, review files across various categories, digitise records, weed out obsolete files and strengthen record management practices. These measures aim to streamline administrative processes, optimise the use of office space and promote efficient functioning.
Promoting Cleanliness across School Campuses
Spearheaded by Eco Clubs for Mission LiFE, schools across the country are undertaking cleanliness drives to maintain clean and hygienic campuses. These efforts aim to strengthen a culture of cleanliness and collective responsibility among students and school staff to create healthier learning environments.
Strengthening e-Waste Awareness and Collection in Schools
As part of Special Campaign 6 and under the aegis of Eco Clubs for Mission LiFE, e-waste awareness and collection drives are being undertaken in schools across the nation to sensitise students and teachers to the importance of responsible e-waste management.
The activities focus on raising awareness about the environmental impact of electronic waste and encouraging students to become active participants in e-waste management by reducing electronic waste and ensuring that discarded equipment is disposed of through authorized channels.
These efforts seek to nurture environmentally conscious behaviour among students and strengthen the role of schools in promoting sustainable practices.
Installation of e-waste bins and Murals at Kartavya Bhavan 2
To mark the International e-waste Day on October 14, 2026, DoSEL installed a creative e-waste mural and e-waste bins at Kartavya Bhavan 2. The mural is made from 50 kg e-waste collected by school students. Aligned with the vision of the
National Education Policy 2020
and
Eco Clubs for Mission LiFE
, the mural promotes the message of “Reduce, Reuse and Recycle”. The bins provide a designated facility for collecting discarded electronic items and reinforce the importance of appropriate e-waste management in institutional settings.
Commitment to Environment Friendliness
Secretary, DoSEL, Shri T. K. Anil Kumar chaired a video conference with States/UTs and autonomous bodies on October 16, 2026 to review preparations for the
nationwide e-waste awareness and collection drive scheduled on October 28, 2026.
The Secretary briefed the participants about the activities to be carried out including the IEC campaign and emphasized upon chalking out a plan for handing over the e-waste collected in schools to authorized vendors.
By combining school-level cleanliness drives with e-waste awareness and collection initiatives under the aegis of Eco Clubs for Mission LiFE, Special Campaign 6 reinforces the importance of collective action in building clean, environmentally responsible educational institutions.

title: STPI Tech Conclave highlights AI's Potential in Healthcare & Assistive Technologies
subtitle: Programme brings together government, academia, healthcare experts and startups to explore AI applications in health, inclusion and well-being
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 OCT 2026 10:59AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Software Technology Parks of India (STPI), a premier S&T organization under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), and the Centre for Innovation, Incubation and Entrepreneurship (CIIE), IIT BHU, organised a Tech Conclave on
“AI for Health & Assistive Technologies”
at IIT BHU, Varanasi. The programme brought together government representatives, academic experts, healthcare professionals and startups to explore how artificial intelligence can advance healthcare, improve accessibility and support inclusion and citizen well-being through practical, scalable solutions.
The inaugural session commenced with the ceremonial lighting of the lamp, followed by welcome remarks by Prof. Manoj Kumar Meshram, Faculty In-Charge, CIIE, IIT BHU. The session featured a keynote address by Shri S. Krishnan, Secretary, MeitY, Government of India, followed by special addresses from Shri Arvind Kumar, Director General, STPI, and Prof. Amit Patra, Director, IIT BHU. Special addresses were also delivered by Shri Sumit Mahajan, CEO, Uttar Pradesh Startup Mission, IT & Electronics Department, Government of Uttar Pradesh, and Dr. Mallika Tiwari, Professor, Department of Oncology, Institute of Medical Sciences, BHU.
Delivering the keynote address, Shri S. Krishnan, Secretary, MeitY, Government of India, said, “Artificial Intelligence can play an important role in making healthcare more accessible, strengthening clinical decision-making and improving service delivery, particularly for communities with limited access to healthcare services. He emphasised the need to integrate AI education across disciplines and leverage the convergence of technology, medical sciences and research to develop practical solutions. He underscored AI's transformative potential in improving healthcare accessibility, affordability and quality through applications such as disease screening, medical diagnostics, remote ICU monitoring and AI-assisted surgical planning. He encouraged stronger collaboration among IIT (BHU), STPI, industry and startups to develop scalable healthcare and assistive technology solutions. He also highlighted the support available through the IndiaAI Mission and other MeitY initiatives, while emphasising STPI's role in connecting startups with investors, venture capital networks and market opportunities to build a sustainable innovation ecosystem.
Shri Arvind Kumar, Director General, STPI, reflected on the transformation of India's technology ecosystem over the past three decades. Highlighting STPI's pivotal role in facilitating the growth of India's IT/ITeS industry since 1991, he emphasised the opportunity to replicate this success in Artificial Intelligence through indigenous innovation and entrepreneurship. Recalling how students earlier primarily aspired to secure campus placements, he noted that today's startup ecosystem enables young innovators to become job creators. Highlighting STPI's industry linkages and 27 Centres of Entrepreneurship, he underscored the importance of translational research, intellectual property creation and market access. He further emphasised the need to strengthen startup ecosystems beyond established technology hubs, particularly in emerging regions, through closer collaboration among academic institutions such as IIT (BHU), industry and government.
Prof. Amit Patra, Director, IIT BHU, addressing the STPI Tech Conclave on AI for Health & Assistive Technologies, highlighted IIT (BHU)'s efforts to strengthen its startup and entrepreneurship ecosystem through the establishment of the Centre for Innovation, Incubation and Entrepreneurship (CIIE). He emphasised the importance of creating a structured institutional framework to nurture entrepreneurial thinking among students, faculty and aspiring innovators, enabling them to transform innovative ideas into viable startups. He underscored the need to connect aspiring entrepreneurs with multiple funding sources and build a sustainable pipeline of startups, reaffirming IIT (BHU)'s commitment to fostering innovation and technology-driven entrepreneurship.
The conclave also featured two panel discussions
— “Empowering Citizens Through AI: Health, Inclusion & Well-being”
and
“From Innovation to Impact: Translating AI Research into Scalable Healthcare & Assistive Solutions”
bringing together experts from government, academia, healthcare and startups to discuss AI’s potential and its translation into practical, scalable solutions. Vote of Thanks was given by Shri Praveen Kumar Dwivedi, Additional Director and OIC, STPI Lucknow
The first panel discussion, “Empowering Citizens Through AI: Health, Inclusion & Well-being,” featured Prof. Manoj Kumar Meshram, Coordinator, CIIE-IIT BHU; Dr. Sanjay Kumar Singh, Professor, Department of Computer Science and Engineering, IIT BHU; Prof. Avanish Singh Parmar, Professor, Department of Physics, IIT (BHU); Dr. Shiru Sharma, Professor, Department of Biomedical Engineering, IIT BHU; Dr. Ruchi Chawla, Associate Professor, Department of Pharmaceutical Engineering and Technology, IIT BHU; Shri Shahbaz Ahmad, Founder, Arkision AI Pvt. Ltd.; and Shri Amit Kumar Verma, Additional Director, STPI. The discussion focused on the potential of AI to support more accessible and inclusive healthcare and improve citizen well-being. The multidisciplinary participation highlighted the importance of bringing together technological expertise, healthcare-related research and entrepreneurial perspectives to explore solutions that respond to people’s needs.
The second panel discussion, “From Innovation to Impact: Translating AI Research into Scalable Healthcare & Assistive Solutions,” featured Shri Rajeshwar Singh Jenwar, Director, MeitY; Dr. Akash Mishra, Assistant Professor, Centre of Biostatistics, IMS-BHU; Dr. Durgesh Narayan Singh, Scientific Officer, BioNest BHU; Ms. Tripti Verma, Founder, LeminAi; and Shri Shyam Kumar, COO, STPI MedTech Centre of Entrepreneurship at SGPGIMS, Lucknow. The session centred on the journey from research and innovation to practical, scalable solutions in healthcare and assistive technology. The mix of institutional, scientific and startup perspectives underscored the value of collaboration in helping promising ideas move towards real-world application.
The conclave reinforced the importance of collaboration among government, academia, healthcare institutions and startups to harness AI for accessible healthcare, assistive technologies and inclusive well-being. Through continued engagement, research translation and entrepreneurship support, STPI and CIIE, IIT BHU, aim to contribute to an innovation ecosystem that develops practical, responsible and scalable technology solutions for societal needs.
About STPI:
Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) is a premier S&T organization under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), engaged in promoting the IT/ITES industry, innovation, research and development, startups, and product and intellectual property creation in emerging technology domains. These include the Internet of Things, blockchain, artificial intelligence, machine learning, computer vision, robotics, augmented and virtual reality, animation and visual effects, and data science and analytics. STPI supports innovation across domains such as gaming, fintech, agritech, medtech, autonomous and connected mobility, ESDM, cybersecurity, Industry 4.0 and drones.

title: Dr. Abhilaksh Likhi, Union Secretary, Department of Fisheries, Visits Munsyari Coldwater Fisheries Cluster; Interacts with Trout Farmers and Reviews Cluster Development Initiatives
ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 OCT 2026 2:31PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Dr. Abhilaksh Likhi, Secretary, Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Government of India, undertook an official visit to Munsyari, district Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand, on 18 October 2026 to review the progress of coldwater aquaculture development in the Himalayan region.
During the visit, the Secretary interacted with trout farmers at Johar Matsya Swayatt Sehkarita, Namjala Trout Farm, Munsyari, and appreciated the pioneering role of local cooperatives in adopting rainbow trout farming as a sustainable livelihood option. He noted that Munsiyari, with its glacial streams of the Gori Ganga and ideal water temperature, has emerged as a hub for rainbow trout culture, transforming subsistence farming into a semi‑commercial enterprise.Dr. Likhi interacted with trout fish farmers, who shared their experiences and insights on trout farming in the region.
The Government of India has notified 34 fisheries clusters across the country. Pithoragarh has been notified as a Cold Water Fisheries Cluster under PMMSY, with significant potential to strengthen fisheries cooperatives, enhance livelihood opportunities and promote sustainable fisheries development in the Himalayan region.The visit by the Secretary, Department of Fisheries, marks an important step towards further strengthening trout farming in Uttarakhand and other Himalayan regions.The Department of Fisheries, Government of Uttarakhand, is exporting trout to Nepal and supplying trout to the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) under an MoU entered between the Government of Uttarakhand and ITBP.
The Secretary highlighted that coldwater fisheries in hilly states such as Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, Sikkim, and Arunachal Pradesh are of strategic importance for livelihood diversification, nutritional security, and export potential.
He emphasized that the Government of India, under the
Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)
, has invested over ₹2,299 crore in coldwater regions, supporting raceways, hatcheries, feed mills, cold storages, and post‑harvest infrastructure.
India’s coldwater fisheries are concentrated in six hilly states and UTs — Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, Sikkim, and Arunachal Pradesh. These regions, with their glaciated rivers, high‑altitude lakes, and pristine streams, provide ideal ecological conditions for rainbow trout and other high‑value coldwater species. Under PMMSY, more than 5,600 raceways, 54 hatcheries, 293 cold storages, and 260 feed mills have been sanctioned across these states. Trout production has grown six‑fold in the last decade, reaching nearly 5,000 MT annually, with Uttarakhand achieving its first international export to Nepal in June 2026.
In Uttarakhand, projects worth ₹317 crore have been sanctioned, including modern fish markets, landing centres, and an integrated aquapark at Sitarganj. The state has also launched the
Trout Protsahan Yojna
with an outlay of ₹170 crore, aiming to establish 1,500 raceways, 100 mini hatcheries, and 600 cold‑storage facilities by 2028–29.
The Secretary commended the role of
ICAR‑Central Institute of Coldwater Fisheries Research (DCFR), Bhimtal
, in introducing rainbow trout to Munsiyari and providing scientific support in seed production, disease management, and farmer training. He also appreciated the historic achievement of Uttarakhand’s first trout export to Nepal in June 2026, which has opened new avenues for international trade.
The visit also underscored the socio‑economic impact of trout farming in border villages, providing livelihood diversification, eco‑tourism opportunities, and assured institutional market linkages with the Indo‑Tibetan Border Police (ITBP).
He underlined that coldwater aquaculture is not only enhancing farmers’ incomes but also contributing to eco‑tourism, conservation of endangered species like Mahseer, and strengthening border village economies.

title: DRI seizes massive 137 kg consignment of crystal meth; busts coastal drug trafficking network; 4 arrested in Tamil Nadu
subtitle: Major intelligence-led operation foils suspected attempt to smuggle drug to Sri Lanka through maritime route
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 OCT 2026 1:17PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a major crackdown on organised drug trafficking,
in one of the biggest narcotics seizures in Tamil Nadu’s coastal region in recent years
, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has seized
137 kg (gross) crystal methamphetamine, a banned synthetic drug,
from a coastal village in Nagapattinam district, Tamil Nadu.
Acting on specific intelligence, DRI officers conducted an intensive surveillance and enforcement operation during 16–17 October 2026, successfully uncovering a suspected coastal drug-trafficking network attempting to smuggle the narcotic substances to Sri Lanka. The consignment was intended to be smuggled to Sri Lanka through mid-sea transfer.
The value of the seized contraband in the illicit drug market is estimated to be in excess of Rs 100 crore.
The operation followed specific intelligence indicating that a large consignment of narcotic substances had been transported to a coastal location in Nagapattinam district for storage and onward smuggling to Sri Lanka. A subsequent search led to the recovery of
six duffel bags containing 27 silver-foil packets, with each weighing approximately 5 kg were recovered
. The packets contained a white crystalline substance suspected to be methamphetamine of high purity.  The contraband was seized under the provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985.
In a simultaneous search at the premises of the suspected organiser, DRI officers seized
Rs. 10 lakh in cash suspected to represent sale proceeds
. Two four-wheelers and one two-wheeler allegedly used for transporting the narcotic substance were also seized. The operation successfully exposed the drug trafficking network including persons involved in organising the coastal export, transportation, storage and logistics of the consignment. Four persons, have been arrested under the provisions of the NDPS Act, 1985, and remanded to judicial custody.
Through this operation, DRI has not only removed a significant quantity of contraband  drugs from illicit circulation but also successfully dismantled a drug-trafficking network. This major seizure underscores DRI’s sustained efforts and enforcement capabilities in disrupting organised drug-trafficking networks and preventing the use of India’s coastline as a corridor for illicit narcotics trafficking.

content:
NCRTC celebrated ‘Namo Bharat Diwas 2026’, marking three successful years of Namo Bharat operations and a transformative journey in regional mobility on 17th October 2026 in New Delhi. The occasion was graced by Hon’ble Union Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs and Power, Shri Manohar Lal; Hon’ble Union Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu; Secretary, Department of Capital Development, MoHUA, and Chairperson, NCRTC, Smt. D. Thara; and Secretary, Department of Urban Development, Shri Satendra Singh. Managing Director, NCRTC, Shri Shalabh Goel, along with the Directors and senior officials, welcomed the dignitaries.
On this occasion, NCRTC reflected on the remarkable journey of Namo Bharat, highlighting key milestones, initiatives to strengthen multimodal connectivity, first- and last-mile connectivity to enhance the commuter experience, and initiatives such as Solar on Track and the development of a 110 MW captive solar power plant to promote the environmental and financial sustainability of the project. These achievements and the progress made by the project were showcased through a film, highlighting the efforts, innovations and initiatives that continue to shape Namo Bharat’s journey.
Speaking on the occasion, Hon’ble Union Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs and Power, Shri Manohar Lal, said, “Namo Bharat’ is not merely a name; it embodies the spirit of putting the nation first, along with the values of dedication, culture and traditions. Namo Bharat rapid rail is ushering in a new era of regional connectivity in India, giving a new dimension to the future of urban transportation. Since its inauguration by Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 20 October 2023, the 82-km-long Delhi–Ghaziabad–Meerut corridor has recorded over 4.5 crore passenger journeys. This achievement reflects the growing trust of the people in modern, safe and seamless transportation.”
He also added, “I believe that better transportation does not merely reduce distances between cities but also connects people with new opportunities, thereby accelerating regional development and economic progress. I commend all the officers, engineers, technical experts, employees and workers of NCRTC for their dedicated and committed contribution towards realising this ambitious project.”
Namo Bharat operations commenced in October 2023 with the inauguration of the 17-km Priority Section between Sahibabad and Duhai Depot. Post which, the entire corridor was operationalised in a phased manner. On 22 February 2026, Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi dedicated the entire 82-km Namo Bharat corridor to the nation, along with Meerut Metro. Namo Bharat currently serves over 1.1 lakh commuters daily and has recently recorded its highest-ever single-day ridership of around 1.68 lakh. With its fast, frequent and reliable services, Namo Bharat is helping people travel more efficiently, bringing workplaces, educational institutions and economic centres within easier reach and giving commuters greater convenience and more time in their daily lives. Two more priority Namo Bharat corridors i.e. Delhi-Panipat-Karnal and Delhi-Gurugram-Behror are likely to receive the approval soon. Two other corridors, Ghaziabad-Jewar and Noida-Faridabad-Gurgaon, are also in the DPR stage.
The occasion also celebrated the people behind this transformation. Addressing the gathering, Managing Director, NCRTC, Shri Shalabh Goel, said, “NCRTC was established with a vision to develop a modern, safe, reliable and environmentally friendly regional transport system in the country. Today, when we look back, it is a matter of pride to see that we have not limited this vision to paper but have made concrete and remarkable progress towards translating it into reality.” He expressed special gratitude to the families who have stood firmly beside team members through every challenge, acknowledging their unwavering support as an integral part of the organisation’s journey.
The occasion also featured the Annual NCRTC Awards, where employees were felicitated for their exemplary performance during the year. The awardees were recognised for their dedication, and commitment to excellence, acknowledging their invaluable contribution to the successful implementation and operation of Namo Bharat. The awards celebrated not only individual achievements but also the collective spirit and teamwork that continue to drive NCRTC’s journey forward. Adding a vibrant cultural dimension to the celebrations, music and dance performances added colour and energy to the occasion.
The journey of Namo Bharat stands as a testament to the power of modern public transport to bring people closer to opportunities and contribute to a more connected, accessible and sustainable region. With commuters at the heart of its vision, NCRTC remains committed to advancing safe, comfortable, reliable and efficient mobility while continuing to build on the achievements of Namo Bharat for the people of the region.

title: Union Social Justice Empowerment Secretary Shri Sudhansh Pant Visits Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 in Mysuru, Karnataka
subtitle:
Nine Days Mela Features 83 Stalls, Including 80 Stalls Allotted To Artisans, Among Them 37 Women Artisans

12 States, Union Territories Participating in the Mela

Secretary Reiterates Government’s Commitment To Ensure Strong Market Access, Encourage Entrepreneurship And Advance Economic Empowerment Of Disadvantaged Communities
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 OCT 2026 9:29PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Secretary of Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant visited the ongoing Nine Days Shilp Samagam Mela 2026, at Mysuru in Karnataka this evening.
The Mela is being organized by the Ministry through joint partnership of three national corporations under the Ministry namely National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) and the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC), which provide financial assistance to artisans and eligible beneficiaries.
During the visit to
Mysuru Dasara Exhibition Grounds, the Secretary inspected stalls and talked to the Stall Managers and visitors.
The Union Secretary is on a two days official visit to Mysuru to take
comprehensive review of the Ministry’s Schemes, Programmes and Initiatives under implementation, with the Administration. He is also undertaking Site Visits in Mysuru.
Shri Pant said through such initiatives, the Ministry continues to strengthen market access, encourage entrepreneurship and advance the economic empowerment of disadvantaged communities.
The Shilp Samagam Mela continues until October 19 Monday, offering visitors an opportunity to explore India’s traditional crafts and handloom products while supporting the livelihoods of artisans.
A Senior Official in the Ministry said the Mela is underway since October 11 and provides a marketing platform for artisans and beneficiaries from Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs) and Safai Karamcharis, enabling them to showcase their traditional handicrafts, handloom products and other goods to a wider audience.
The Official informed that the ongoing Mela features 83 stalls, including 80 stalls allotted to artisans, among them 37 women artisans. Artisans from 12 States and Union Territories, including Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Kerala, Rajasthan, Puducherry, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh, are participating in the exhibition.
He said the stalls feature with a diverse range of products, including handicrafts, handloom sarees, spices, pickles, incense sticks, honey products, block-printed items, leather goods, wooden toys, bags, purses, terracotta products, artificial jewellery, rosewood wall hangings, and bed and cushion covers. He also visited the Food stalls serving traditional delicacies adding to the visitor experience.
The Official further said the Mela is designed to strengthen market linkages for artisans, promote traditional craftsmanship and create sustainable livelihood opportunities. Through direct interaction with visitors and prospective customers, participating artisans can display their products, expand their customer base and improve the market reach of their enterprises. The initiative also promotes India’s rich cultural heritage and supports the preservation of traditional art forms and skills, he added.
He added that the Mela also serves as an important platform for disseminating information about the schemes and programmes of the Ministry and its three national corporations, helping eligible beneficiaries learn about available financial assistance and entrepreneurship opportunities.
The Official informed that the Ministry facilitates artisans’ participation by providing free stalls and support towards travel expenses, daily allowance, transportation of goods and meals, in accordance with the applicable arrangements.
It is pertinent to mention that in addition to the Mela, the Ministry is promoting the BHARAT TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme) initiative to expand market access for products made by target-group artisans through digital platforms in India and abroad. Branding products under BHARAT TULIP is intended to improve their visibility, facilitate online sales and connect traditional artisans with a wider customer base.
The Ministry has been organizing Shilp Samagam Melas since 2022, benefiting 975 artisans through 13 fairs held so far.
The ongoing Mysuru edition is the first Shilp Samagam Mela of the financial year 2026–27.
The Ministry also proposes to organize additional fairs in Guwahati (Oct 21 to 28, 2026); Dilli Haat in New Delhi, Jodhpur and Lucknow during the current financial year, alongside participation in major exhibitions such as the India International Trade Fair 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, from November 14 to 27, 2026, and the Surajkund Mela in February 2027.

title: India’s Nutrient-Rich Purple Potato
subtitle: Kufri Jamunia: Integrating Nutrition into one of India’s Most Common Staple Crops
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                18 OCT 2026 1:44PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Hidden hunger remains a major nutritional challenge despite adequate calorie intake in many populations.
Biofortified crops
are being developed to improve the intake of essential vitamins and minerals through daily food consumption. In this context,
ICAR-CPRI
(Indian Council of Agricultural Research- Central Potato Research Institute) developed nutrient-rich coloured potato varieties, including
Kufri neelkanth, Kufri manik,
and
Kufri jamunia
. These varieties contain important
antioxidants
and
micronutrients,
such as anthocyanins, iron, and zinc. Among them, Kufri jamunia represents a major advancement due to its higher levels of Vitamin C, anthocyanins, and carotenoids. Its improved nutritional profile, attractive purple flesh, and strong consumer appeal make it an important variety for addressing hidden hunger and improving nutritional security
.
Potatoes Beyond Calories: Addressing Hidden Hunger
Hidden hunger remains a major public health challenge despite adequate calorie intake. It occurs when people consume sufficient food but lack essential vitamins and minerals in their diet. To address this challenge, scientists are increasingly developing
biofortified crops
with enhanced nutritional value. Biofortification
improves the nutrient content
of crops through plant breeding, enabling food to naturally provide higher levels of essential nutrients. Unlike conventional food fortification, which adds nutrients during processing, biofortification
integrates nutrition directly into the crop
. This makes it a sustainable and cost-effective approach to improving nutritional quality in commonly consumed foods. It also strengthens
long-term nutritional security
.
One important outcome of biofortification research has been the development of
coloured potato
varieties with enhanced nutritional value. These include
red, purple
, and
blue
-fleshed potatoes. These potatoes contain
natural pigments,
such as anthocyanins and carotenoids, which give them their distinctive colours. Coloured potatoes are rich in
antioxidants
and micronutrients such as
iron
and
zinc
.
Nutrient-Rich Coloured Potato Varieties Developed by ICAR-CPRI
ICAR-CPRI (Indian Council of Agricultural Research- Central Potato Research Institute) has developed the following nutrient-rich coloured potato varieties:
Kufri Neelkanth
was the first purple-skinned specialty potato variety developed by ICAR-CPRI (Central Potato Research Institute), released in
2018
. The variety is suitable for cultivation in
Punjab
,
Haryana
,
Uttar Pradesh
,
Uttarakhand
,
Bihar
,
Madhya Pradesh,
and
Chhattisgarh
. It is known for its high antioxidant content. The variety is suitable for people of all age groups.
Kufri manik
was released in
2021
. It produces attractive, deep red tubers with a round shape, medium eyes, and yellow flesh. The variety is rich in nutrients and contains high levels of anthocyanin, zinc, and iron.
Kufri jamunia
was officially released in
2024
. The variety contains
higher levels of ascorbic acid, anthocyanin, and carotenoids
than
Kufri manik
and
Kufri neelkanth
. Its purple flesh indicates high antioxidant content and better nutritional quality.
Kufri jamunia
also contains
enhanced levels of zinc and iron.
The variety is suitable for table purposes and adds novelty to different food preparations due to its unique purple colour. Hence, this variety is observed to have very high consumer appeal.
Kufri jamunia
: A Biofortified Purple Potato for Nutritional Security
Kufri jamunia
is a medium-maturing potato variety with medium-tall plants and a semi-compact canopy. The tubers are dark purple on the skin and purple in the flesh. They are oblong, with shallow eyes and a mealy texture. Each plant produces 10–12 medium to large tubers.
Salient characteristics of
Kufri jamunia
are:
• Produces
32-35 tonnes per hectare
under recommended cultivation practices.
• Recorded around
49 tonnes per hectare yield
in station trials at 90 days duration.
• Marketable yield reached nearly
90%
of total production in trials.
• Shows
medium dormancy
of around 6-8 weeks. Hence, tubers do not sprout quickly.
• Possesses good storage quality with
low rottage
and
minimal weight loss
.
Key Nutritional Components in
Kufri Jamunia
Kufri jamunia
contains 42.05 mg/100 g of anthocyanins in flesh and 80.66 mg/100 g in skin. It also contains around 42.75 mg/100 g of
Vitamin C
in the flesh. The
carotenoid
content is around 161 µg/100 g fresh weight in flesh. In addition, the variety contains about 22.77 ppm
zinc
and 32.23 ppm
iron
in the flesh. The following table compares the nutritional value of
Kufri jamunia
with conventional yellow-skinned potato:
Nutrient (per 100 gm)
Kufri Jamunia
Common Potato
Vitamin C
42.75 mg
23.15 mg
Zinc
2.28 mg
0.28 mg
Iron
3.22 mg
0.57 mg
Culinary Uses of
Kufri jamunia
Apart from its nutritional advantages,
Kufri jamunia
is suitable for a wide range of culinary applications. The variety is valued for its
attractive purple colour, mealy texture, and pleasant flavour
. This makes it suitable for both traditional preparations and processed food products. Its distinctive pigmentation also enhances the visual appeal of dishes and processed foods.
Purple-fleshed potatoes such as
Kufri jamunia
can be used in several preparations, including:
Traditional dishes:
vegetable curry, paratha, puri, and raita
Breakfast and snack preparations:
daliya, halwa, upma, dosa, and idli batter
Processed products:
potato flour for bakery items, soups, and cookies
In addition, the tubers can be processed into
dehydrated products
such as
anthocyanin-rich daliya, suji, and flour
, which can be used as ingredients in various food formulations.
States Suitable for
Kufri jamunia
Cultivation
For large-scale adoption, a crop variety must perform reliably across different agro-climatic conditions.
Kufri jamunia
has demonstrated stable performance in multi-location trials and has been recommended for cultivation in the
North Indian plains
. The variety is considered suitable for several states where potatoes are widely grown.
These regions provide
favourable climatic
and
soil conditions
for the successful cultivation of this variety.
The Nutritional and Agricultural Promise of
Kufri jamunia
Kufri jamunia
represents an
important advancement in the development of biofortified potato varieties in India
. By combining good agronomic performance with enhanced nutritional quality, the variety offers benefits for both farmers and consumers. Its rich content of antioxidants, vitamins, and micronutrients makes it a valuable addition to efforts to improve dietary diversity and address hidden hunger. With its attractive appearance, culinary versatility, and adaptability to several states in the North Indian plains,
Kufri jamunia
has strong potential for wider cultivation and consumption in the future.
